newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Riviera doctors strike over health reforms.
newsitem.headline: French Riviera doctors strike over health reforms.

text.p: Hundreds of doctors went on strike in southern France on Monday to protest against planned reforms of the national health system which they say will unfairly tax them.
The Maritime Alps department, whose main city is Nice, capital of the French Riviera, has an estimated 3,500 doctors or 313 for every 100,000 inhabitants, the highest rate in France.
Up to 95 percent of specialists in certain fields and about 60 percent of general practitioners kept their cabinets closed much of the day, doctors unions said.

Doctors are furious at government plans which they say will make them pay between 6,000 and 100,000 francs ($1,200 and $20,000) if national health expenses go over budget next year. The figures vary according to regions.

France has a massive 33 billion franc ($6 billion) national health deficit this year which officials largely attribute to specialists ordering unneeded tests and doctors prescribing too many pharmaceutical products.
Health care is generously reimbursed in France by a national health system to which most people contribute.
The government is also seeking to cap many fees charged by doctors and the medical profession has called for nationwide protests between November 7 and 11.
